messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: disabling *all* data transformations?
parts:
Hi!

Is it possible to disable *all* data manipulations from RStanArm?

I learned that I need to use autoscale=FALSE to avoid any scaling, but then I am left with automatic centering. At least this is what the prior_summary function tells me (or I understand it as such).

So how can I avoid that RStanArm does any scaling or centering for me such that the priors have their actual meaning as specified?

I know that scaling and centering are really important, but I much prefer to do that myself. Using means and standard deviations from the data is only a quick and dirty solution to me, I prefer to center and scale using meaningful references which are problem specific.

Many thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: disabling *all* data transformations?
parts:
On Thursday, March 30, 2017 at 6:07:31 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
I know that scaling and centering are really important, but I much prefer to do that myself. Using means and standard deviations from the data is only a quick and dirty solution to me, I prefer to center and scale using meaningful references which are problem specific.

I think the only way to avoid centering is to specify sparse = TRUE, which will probably make it slower. But if you have strong prior beliefs about the intercept with the original predictors, it should be straightforward to figure out what your prior beliefs are when the predictors are centered.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] disabling *all* data transformations?
parts:
Are you worried that standardizing data leads to
data-specific priors? I think you wind up getting very
similar results as to not transforming, but I'd like
to see that better formalized and I'd like to know roughly
how much data you need before the empirical standardization
on a specific sample converges within whatever tolerance
you have to not standardizing.

So in a simple case,

Y ~ normal(alpha + X * beta, sigma);

where x and y are realization of the random variables
X and Y, then the sample standardization

z = (x - mean(x)) / sd(x)

should converge as the size of x grows (assuming x is well behaved)
to (X - E[X]) / sd[X].

I just don't know how fast that's going to happen.

If you have weakly informative priors on alpha and beta,
then it probably won't make much of a difference because the
prior sensitivity will be similarly weak if the data is
consistent with the prior.

So I think Ben's just saying that you can transform your
priors based based on the expected standardization of X and Y,
and you should be OK. To do that, of course, you need
to know E[X], sd[X], E[Y], and sd[Y].

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] disabling *all* data transformations?
parts:
I simply don't want to give away control. There can be good reasons to not standardize using the data at hand, but to some other rationale. Whatever other rationale used should be close to the usual data standardization, yes, but there can be situations when this differs.

rstanarm was probably built for the "weak" prior regime and works-out-of-the-box using defaults. However, to me one of the biggest advantages from using Bayesian inference is whenever data is sparse or I can use informative prios. Hence, I *want* that my prior shows up in the analysis. In that case things matter.

I am just used by now to try to understand what is my model saying, i.e. what is my reference and what is my scale telling me. Its already hard enough for me to figure that out; and now I also need to take rstanarm arms magic into account... but maybe that's a personal preference and I belong to those 5% of users quoted earlier...

Anyway, as I understand Ben, I can always figure out my priors by shifting the prior by the data mean to get what I want. I would really prefer an option in rstanarm which allows me to disable all internal magic. How about an extra argument to the priors? In addition to autoscale an autocenter option?

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] disabling *all* data transformations?
parts:
I have the same preferences, but that exact level of
control isn't (and I'd argue shouldn't be) the goal
of RStanArm---we have RStan for that.

I also think features should be added with great care
so as not to complicate a product. Each addition makes
the doc bigger and makes the whole harder to understand.
Horses for courses, as the bettors say.

I don't have an opinion on this particular feature for
RStanArm. Sometimes the added complexity (and *any*
option is added complexity) is worth it.

I think if you actually have priors (that is prior to
the data), then you'll need to see the data and convert
to the equivalent prior after seeing the data.

- Bob
